title: Determinant of a block lower-triangular matrix
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $p,q\ge0$ integers and $M$ a $(p+q)\times(p+q)$ matrix with entries in $R$ which in block form is $M=\begin{pmatrix}P&0\\C&Q\end{pmatrix}$, with $P$ a $p\times p$ matrix (rows and columns $1,\dots,p$), $Q$ a $q\times q$ matrix (rows and columns $p+1,\dots,p+q$), $C$ a $q\times p$ matrix and the upper right $p\times q$ block zero, i.e. $M_{ij}=0$ for $i\le p<j$. Then $\det M=\det P\cdot\det Q$ (an empty determinant being $1$).
